perf_tips:
More latency tips:
• Use a dedicated 5 GHz / 6 GHz WiFi (headset as the only client, PC on LAN cable)
• Streaming tab: prefer the hardware encoder (vaapi/nvenc) instead of x264
• H.265/AV1 at 80–120 Mbps is usually smoother than H.264 at very high bitrates
• Foveated encoding reduces encode time — 50% is a good start
• Set your GPU power profile to performance while playing
killcmd_desc: The Kill apps button on the dashboard already terminates all autostart programs the normal way (SIGTERM → SIGKILL). Some apps ignore that though — Electron apps (VRCX) fork into several processes, some AppImages run under a different process name, and a few tools want to be closed with their own command. Add such special cases here: they run in addition to the normal kill, right before it.

Reset restores the source that was active before.

ubuntu_guide_text:
WiVRn isn't in the Ubuntu/Debian repositories, so it has to be built once from source.

A native build is leaner and performs better than a sandboxed one — it talks to your GPU and USB devices directly, with no sandbox overhead.

Click 'Copy commands', paste them into a terminal and let it run (10–20 minutes). After that, restart yakuda-connect and everything else works as usual.

Afterwards you'll have:
  • wivrn-server in your PATH
  • OpenComposite in /opt/opencomposite (for VRChat and other OpenVR games)

    sudo dnf install -y {name}

one after the other. All you do there is enter your sudo password — nothing to copy.

Note: OpenComposite comes from the official repos and is perfectly fine for VRChat. {name} is optional and gives better performance in many games.

oxr_doc_text:
One or more OpenXR runtime manifests on this system point to a library that does not exist or has the wrong architecture (32 vs 64 bit).

Steam reads every one of these files at startup inside its container. A bad entry makes steamwebhelper crash in a loop with "invalid `Elf' handle" — Steam then won't start at all.

{items}

Repair now? The affected files are backed up with a timestamp first; paths are corrected where possible, otherwise the file is disabled (renamed to .disabled). Administrator rights may be requested.

exit_group_desc:
Decides what happens to the WiVRn server when yakuda-connect ends.

On (default): the server is stopped exactly like switching it off on the dashboard — including autostart programs and custom kill commands. This applies to every way of ending the app: the window's X, closing from the taskbar, ending it in a task manager/resource monitor, and pkill.

A hard kill (kill -9, "Kill process", a crash) is covered as well: while the server runs, a small helper process (yakuda-guard) watches and cleans up if the app suddenly disappears.

Off: the server keeps running after closing, as it did up to v1.2.9.
exit_stop_server_tip: On by default. When yakuda-connect closes (also via taskbar, task manager or pkill), the server is stopped like switching it off on the dashboard.

games_info_title: Proton version & launch options in Steam
games_info_text:
Change the Proton version of a game:
1. Open Steam and right-click the game in your library
2. Properties… → Compatibility
3. Check Force the use of a specific Steam Play compatibility tool
4. Pick the recommended version from the dropdown (e.g. installed via ProtonPlus)
5. If a freshly installed version is missing from the list: restart Steam first

Set launch options:
1. Right-click the game → Properties… → General
2. Paste the copied launch options into the Launch Options field at the bottom

Tip: the Copy buttons on each game card put the right values into your clipboard.

No active firewall was found on this system (that is normal on Arch/CachyOS, for example), so nothing needs to be opened here.

If your headset still cannot find the PC, the block is elsewhere — usually the router, a guest/IoT WiFi that isolates clients, or a VPN.

firewall_manual_text:
This system uses {fw}. Rules there depend on your table and chain names, so the app does not change them automatically — a wrong rule can cut the machine off the network.

Run these commands yourself:
streaming_openvr_off_tip: Writes null. OpenVR games (VRChat and others) will not start through WiVRn — only useful with SteamVR.
streaming_openvr_custom_tip: Pick your own folder — for self-built installations outside the usual locations.
streaming_openvr_rescan_tip: Search again for installed OpenVR compatibility layers
streaming_openvr_active_off: Currently in WiVRn's config: null — WiVRn does not touch OpenVR.
streaming_openvr_active_broken: the folder holds no OpenVR library
streaming_openvr_write_failed:
WiVRn's config.json could not be written.

File: {path}
usb_state_ready: {name} connected — auto connect via USB will work.
usb_state_unauthorized: {name} connected, but this PC is not confirmed yet. Put on the headset and allow USB debugging.
usb_state_usb_only: {name} connected, but not reachable via adb. Enable USB debugging in the headset.
usb_state_no_adb: {name} connected, but adb is missing. Install the Android tools in the Tools tab.
dashboard_apk_meta: Quest users can also get WiVRn straight from the Meta Horizon Store — no cable, no USB debugging: {link}
dashboard_apk_meta_link: Open WiVRn in the Meta Store
streaming_openvr_default_tip: Removes the key from WiVRn's config.json. WiVRn would currently use: {path}
streaming_openvr_outside_tip: Found, but outside WiVRn's own search path — only works because the path is written explicitly.
streaming_openvr_active_default: Currently in WiVRn's config: nothing set — WiVRn picks: {path}
streaming_openvr_restart_hint: Takes effect the next time the WiVRn server starts.
refresh_where: The refresh rate is set in the headset, not on the PC: WiVRn app → settings, or press both thumbsticks while streaming. WiVRn's server configuration has no key for it.
games_fix_pictures_tip:
Links the VRChat pictures folder inside the Proton prefix to your Linux pictures folder.
VRChat screenshots then show up directly in ~/Pictures/VRChat — no more digging through
compatdata/438100/pfx/...

An existing real folder is backed up as VRChat_backup first.
games_fix_video_tip: About VRCVideoCacher — helps when YouTube videos won't play in worlds.
games_fix_check_tip:
Checks Proton version, launch options, system clock, VRChat's Tools folder and the
last playback attempt in the log — and shows what's wrong.
games_video_fix_text:
YouTube videos not playing in worlds?

Typical in-game message:
“Loading failed. File not found, codec not supported, video resolution too high or insufficient system resources.”

The URL usually resolves fine — only playback fails, because YouTube ties the address to the client that requested it. When the video player then fetches it itself, the server rejects it.

VRCVideoCacher fixes this by downloading the video itself and serving it to VRChat locally. It replaces VRChat's yt-dlp on startup and restores it on exit.

Check these first — they're free:
• System clock in sync? If the clock is off, the signed video URLs are already expired. The “Video Player Check” covers this.
• RTSP Proton selected? Without the MediaFoundation patches AVPro plays almost nothing on Linux.

About the Google account: You only need the browser extension — and therefore a Google account — against YouTube's bot detection (“Sign in to confirm you're not a bot”). For the error described here it is not required, so try VRCVideoCacher without cookies first. If you do need it, the developers explicitly recommend a secondary account rather than your main one.

Linux setup: requires dotnet-runtime-10.0. By default VRCVideoCacher downloads its own binaries, so there's nothing else to do.
games_check_failed: ✘ Check failed — see the log for details.
games_check_head_err: ✘ {n} item(s) are very likely the cause.
vrccheck_prefix_hint: Not found. Launch VRChat through Steam once.
vrccheck_proton_hint: Videos fail with this build. RTSP builds carry extra MediaFoundation patches that let AVPro play — switch to the recommended version in the list above.
vrccheck_launch_hint: --enable-avpro-in-proton is missing. Without it most video players stay silent. It's already part of the recommended parameters above.
vrccheck_clock_hint: Clock not synchronized. Video URLs are signed and time-limited — if the clock is off they count as expired immediately. Fix: sudo timedatectl set-ntp true
vrccheck_tools_hint: yt-dlp.exe missing. VRChat creates it on login — sign in to the game once.
vrccheck_ytdlp_hint: Not installed. VRChat doesn't need it, but VRCVideoCacher can use it.
vrccheck_cacher_hint: Not running. See “Video Player Fix” if videos won't play.
vrccheck_video_hint: Playback failed even though the URL resolved — exactly the case VRCVideoCacher is meant for. See “Video Player Fix”.
vrccheck_norun_hint: VRChat isn't running — check while in-game for full results.
games_toggle_proton_log_tip: Writes a verbose Proton log to ~/steam-438100.log — the only place that shows WHY a video player fails (mfplat, GStreamer, codec). Enable for troubleshooting only: the log grows large fast. Environment variable — goes before %command%.
backup_cfg_btn_tip:
Backs up the game's data from the Proton prefix (settings, saves) to
~/.config/yakuda-connect/games_backup/

For VRChat, screenshots are also copied to ~/Pictures/VRChat_backup/.
restore_cfg_btn_none: No backup yet. Use “Back up config” first.
backup_cfg_text:
When you switch Proton versions, Steam often creates a fresh prefix — settings and saves for {game} would be gone.

Back up now? ({files} files, about {size} MB)
backup_cfg_large: Note: that's quite a lot. This may take a while.
backup_cfg_nothing: Nothing to back up — the Proton prefix doesn't exist yet. Launch the game through Steam once.
restore_cfg_text:
Backup from {created}, created under {proton} — {files} files.

Nothing is deleted: existing files are set aside as “.vor-restore” first.
restore_cfg_no_prefix: The Proton prefix doesn't exist yet. Launch the game through Steam once — only then does Proton create the environment to restore into.
vrccheck_proton_works: Not an RTSP build, but it demonstrably plays on your system. Nothing to do.
vrccheck_proton_untested: Not an RTSP build. No playback attempt in the log yet — play a video once and check again. RTSP builds are the safe choice, but not the only one that works.
vci_done_desktop: Shortcut added to the application menu. The autostart switch is now usable.
vci_failed_notbinary: ✘ The download wasn't a Linux binary. Probably a network problem or the release was renamed — please download manually from GitHub.
dashboard_vci_btn_tip:
Starts or stops VRCVideoCacher — fixes YouTube videos that won't play in worlds.

Best started BEFORE VRChat: it swaps out VRChat's yt-dlp and restores it on exit.
dashboard_vci_started:
VRCVideoCacher is running.

Start VRChat now. Press the same button again to stop it — VRChat's yt-dlp is then restored cleanly.
dashboard_vci_stopped: VRCVideoCacher stopped. VRChat's yt-dlp has been restored.
dashboard_vci_not_installed:
VRCVideoCacher isn't installed.

Games tab → VRChat → “Video Player Fix” → “Set up automatically”.
games_vci_note: ℹ Recommended: start VRCVideoCacher from the Dashboard before launching VRChat. Autostarting it via launch options proved unreliable and was removed.
adv_mode_tip: Shows technical details for actions that change something on your system: affected files, required permissions and the matching terminal command to copy. Nothing is executed automatically, and no feature behaves differently — only the extra information appears.
adv_perm_home: write access in your home directory
adv_perm_root_maybe: root via pkexec only if the file belongs to root
adv_fw_explain: Adds a rule to the firewall that is active on this system ({fw}) so the headset can reach the WiVRn server: port {port} TCP and UDP for the connection itself, port {mdns} UDP (mDNS) so the headset can find the PC in the first place. The ports are opened for wivrn-server, not for yakuda-connect.
adv_fw_no_firewall_cmd: # no active firewall found — nothing needs to be opened
adv_oxr_explain: Writes active_runtime.json with absolute paths to the WiVRn libraries. The previous file is kept as .bak with a timestamp.
adv_rt_explain: Points active_runtime.json at WiVRn or at SteamVR. When switching to SteamVR the OpenVR compatibility in WiVRn's config.json is set to disabled and the previous value is remembered for switching back.
adv_prio_explain: Grants the wivrn-server binary the CAP_SYS_NICE capability so reprojection can run at high priority. This is a capability on one file — not a permanently elevated process. It has to be re-applied after a WiVRn update.
adv_wayvr_explain: Downloads the design by cubee-cb from GitHub and copies it to ~/.config/wayvr. The existing folder is backed up beforehand.
adv_osc_explain: Sets one key in the config file of each supported program ({keys}). All other keys stay untouched, and files that do not exist yet are not created.
adv_backup_explain: Copies the current VR configuration into a folder inside your home directory. Reads system folders, but changes nothing outside your home directory.
adv_restore_explain: Copies the backup back. This is the only action that also writes to /usr and /opt — that part runs via pkexec and creates a timestamped backup first. Nothing is deleted; existing files are moved aside.
adv_server_explain: Starts the wivrn-server process as your user and stops it again. Its output goes to a log file in your cache folder.
adv_update_explain: About 1.5 seconds after start, yakuda-connect reads one file from GitHub and compares the version number in it with the installed one. Nothing is sent along except the request itself — no identifier, no system information.
adv_diag_explain: The log is written locally and never sent anywhere. It is only passed on if you copy or save it yourself.
firewall_info:
Open WiVRn ports

Port 9757 (TCP and UDP) carries the connection between the WiVRn server on this PC and the VR headset. Port 5353 (UDP, mDNS) is what lets the headset find the PC — without it the server list in the headset stays empty even when 9757 is open.

The ports are opened for wivrn-server. yakuda-connect itself does not listen on any port. They are not used for telemetry, analytics or data collection.

Only the firewall that is actually active on this system is changed (firewalld or ufw). nftables and iptables are detected but never modified automatically — you get the commands to copy.
streaming_enc_auto: WiVRn picks automatically: nvenc on Nvidia, otherwise vaapi, otherwise x264.
streaming_enc_nvenc: Nvidia hardware encoding — for Nvidia GPUs.
streaming_enc_vaapi: Hardware encoding — for AMD and Intel GPUs.
streaming_enc_vulkan: Vulkan video encode — works on any GPU that supports it. Marked experimental by WiVRn, and only h264/h265, no AV1.
streaming_enc_x264: Software encoding on the CPU — works everywhere, but costs the most CPU and only does h264. A fallback when no hardware encoder works.
streaming_encoder_tip:
Which chip compresses the video stream.

• nvenc — Nvidia GPUs
• vaapi — AMD and Intel GPUs
• Vulkan — any GPU with Vulkan video encode (experimental)
• x264 — software encoding on the CPU

Auto leaves the choice to WiVRn and is the right setting for almost everyone. Picking an encoder your GPU does not have stops the server from starting.
design_desc: Pick a theme, recolour anything you like, or drop an image behind the window.
design_hint: A theme recolours the whole interface. Green and yellow stay as they are on purpose — they mean "running" and "attention".
apt_ppa_title: Install WiVRn from the LVRA PPA?
apt_ppa_text:
WiVRn is not in the official Ubuntu sources; it lives in the Linux VR Adventures project's PPA:

    {ppa}

A PPA is a third-party repository. It stays active after the installation and will also supply updates for WiVRn.

Choosing 'Yes' opens a terminal that adds the PPA, refreshes the package lists and installs WiVRn, one after the other. All you do there is enter your sudo password.

Note: Steam games additionally need xrizer, which the PPA does not carry — it is fetched straight from the GitHub release instead (no repository, no root).
apt_ppa_yes: Yes, add the PPA and install
install_apt_missing: ⚠ Not installed: {pkgs}. Check apt's output in the terminal — usually the PPA has no build for this Ubuntu release.
apt_ppa_unsupported_title: PPA has no build for this Ubuntu release
apt_ppa_unsupported_text:
The PPA {ppa} carries no packages for "{codename}" — the base of this distribution.

Adding it would fail with "Cannot add PPA: This PPA does not support {codename}", so it isn't attempted.

WiVRn is available as a Flatpak from Flathub instead. It runs on any distribution and ships xrizer and OpenComposite with it, so no extra download is needed.

Worth knowing: the Flatpak runs in a sandbox. SteamVR lighthouse trackers don't work with it, the configuration lives under ~/.var/app/, and controlling the server from yakuda-connect is limited.
apt_flatpak_missing:
Flatpak is not installed on this system.

    sudo apt install flatpak

Then try again.
native_guide_text:
On Debian, Ubuntu and Linux Mint, yakuda-connect does not automate the native route — there are too many differences per release: the PPA does not build for every Ubuntu version, an OpenVR translation layer is missing there anyway, and OpenComposite would have to be built by hand.

The guide walks through the native installation step by step.

Afterwards there is nothing else to do here: as soon as wivrn-server is in your PATH, yakuda-connect picks it up on its own, no matter where it came from.
games_manual_note: Not distributed through the AUR or ProtonPlus — the button downloads the build from the GitHub release, verifies its SHA-512 checksum and extracts it into compatibilitytools.d.
games_manual_restart_steam:
{tool} has been extracted into compatibilitytools.d.

Please restart Steam — only then will the version show up in the compatibility settings and can be applied with “Use”.
games_toggle_proton_use_wayland_tip: Puts PROTON_USE_WAYLAND=1 in front of the launch command, switching on the native Wayland path instead of running through XWayland. Only has an effect on Proton builds that carry the WineWayland patches (e.g. Proton-RTSP-Wayland-GE) — other builds ignore the variable. Note: on the Wayland path Xalia is off and Steam Input defaults to off.
autostart_apps_tip: Lists every program installed through the Tools tab.
autostart_apps_hint: Programs and OSC apps installed on this system. Picking one puts its launch command into the row (double-click applies directly).
autostart_apps_none: No program from the Tools tab is installed yet. Install one there first, or type the command by hand.
autostart_profile_add_tip: New autostart profile with a condition (e.g. “when VRChat runs”)
autostart_profile_delete_q: Delete profile “{name}”? Running programs of this profile will be closed.
autostart_profile_pick_tip: Pick from the programs running right now
autostart_profile_pick_hint: Start the program (e.g. VRChat) and pick it here. Double-click applies directly.
autostart_profile_delay_tip: Waits after detection before starting the programs — lets e.g. VRChat load in peace first (performance).
autostart_profile_stop_with_tip: When the trigger exits, this profile's programs are closed too.
autostart_profile_timer_tip: Timer on: starts the programs automatically as soon as the trigger runs. Timer off: only via “Start programs”.
autostart_profile_start_now_tip: Starts the programs below right away — without waiting for the trigger.
autostart_profile_games_tip: Pick a game from the Games tab as trigger
autostart_profile_games_hint: All games from the Games tab. Steam games are detected by their AppId — no matter what the .exe is called. Double-click applies directly.
autostart_profile_games_none: The Games tab has no games yet. Open it once to scan, or type the program name by hand.
autostart_profile_status_off: Timer off — programs only via “Start programs”.
tools_filter_empty: Nothing matches the search and filters. Clear the search box or set category/status back to “All”.
netbuffers_info:
Enlarge the UDP buffers for WiVRn

WiVRn pushes the video over UDP. If the kernel's socket buffer is smaller than a frame, the kernel drops packets before WiVRn ever sees them — which shows up as stutter, blocky artefacts or short dropouts, especially at high bitrate and resolution.

The target is 25 MiB (26214400 bytes), the value named in the WiVRn documentation. Only net.core.rmem_max and net.core.wmem_max are changed. The *_default values are left alone — those apply to every socket on the system, not just the video stream.

Asks for your password once (pkexec).
netbuffers_ask_text:
Current: {current}
Target:  {target} bytes (25 MiB) for both

How long should this apply?

• Permanently — creates {path} and sets the values right away. Survives a reboot.
• This session only — sets the values right away, writes no file. Back to the old values after a reboot.

Either way you are asked for your password once.
netbuffers_ok_session:
Network buffers set to {target} bytes.

This only lasts until the next reboot. If it helped, press the button again and choose “Permanently”.
netbuffers_fail_text:
Setting them automatically did not work ({err}).

These commands do the same thing in a terminal:
dashboard_connect_tip: Starts the connection over the cable, exactly like the WiVRn dashboard does: set up the adb tunnel and launch the WiVRn app on the headset.
dashboard_connect_tip_nousb:
No headset reachable via adb. Check the cable and enable USB debugging.

Over Wi-Fi the PC cannot initiate the connection — there you press "Connect" inside the headset.
dashboard_connect_tip_noserver: The WiVRn server is not running. Start the server above first.
dashboard_apk_download_tip: Downloads the matching APK into a folder of your choice without installing it — for SideQuest, a USB stick or installing later.
apk_choose_folder: Choose a folder for the APK
apk_no_adb: ⚠ android-tools is not installed — add it from the Tools tab. Downloading only works without adb.
apk_status_lookup: Looking for the release matching your installed server...
apk_status_no_release: Error: no release with an APK found (network or GitHub rate limit?).
apk_match_server: Matching your server {server}: WiVRn {tag} — starting download...
apk_no_match_server: ⚠ No release matches server {server} — downloading {tag} instead. Client and server must match or the headset will not connect. For git builds the matching APK lives at github.com/WiVRn/WiVRn-APK.
apk_server_unknown: Server version unknown — downloading the latest release {tag}.
apk_status_bad_file: Error: the downloaded file is not an APK. Is a captive portal in the way?
apk_status_no_headset: No headset found! Enable USB debugging and check the cable.
usb_connect_running: Connecting over the cable... (press the button again to cancel)
usb_connect_ok: ✔ Connection started ({package}) — put the headset on.
usb_connect_no_device: No headset reachable via adb — check the cable and USB debugging.
usb_connect_no_package_short: No WiVRn app installed on the headset.
usb_connect_no_package:
The headset could not match the connection to any app.

Every known WiVRn package name was tried, plus the URL scheme route — so WiVRn really does seem to be missing.

Install it via "Download & install APK" in the Installation tab, or from your headset's store.
adb_fix_tip: Restarts the adb server. Needed after android-tools was updated: /usr/bin/adb is new, but the running server is still the old one.
adb_fix_confirm:
The adb server will be stopped and started again.

Running adb connections will drop, including those of other programs such as SideQuest. The headset may ask for "Allow USB debugging" again afterwards — best to put it on.

Continue?
adb_fix_confirm_udev:
adb reports missing permissions, so the udev rules need to be reloaded.

This will ask for your password. The adb server is restarted afterwards; running adb connections will drop.

Continue?
adb_fix_ok: ✔ adb is talking to the headset again.
adb_fix_failed: The handshake is still not working.
adb_fix_step_restart_failed: The adb server would not start — is another program holding it (SideQuest, Android Studio), or is it running as a different user (started via sudo)?
adb_fix_step_udev_failed: The udev rules could not be reloaded (password prompt cancelled?).
adb_fix_step_install: adb is not installed — add android-tools from the Tools tab.
adb_fix_step_confirm: The headset is asking now: put it on and tap "Allow". Ticking "Always allow from this computer" avoids the prompt next time.
adb_fix_step_still_broken: adb still does not see the headset. Replug the cable (ideally a different port), unlock the headset and check USB debugging in the developer settings.
usb_state_after_update: — android-tools has been updated since the last working access ({old} → {new}); restarting the adb server usually fixes this.
usb_state_mtp_busy: — an MTP session is also open (file manager); close that window, some headsets do not allow MTP and adb at the same time.
usb_connect_ok_generic: ✔ Connection started — put the headset on.
usb_connect_waiting: Waiting for the PICO... If it stays stuck: on the headset, switch the USB option briefly to "Charge only" and back to "File transfer" — that resets the interface.
usb_connect_probably: ✔ The start command went out — the headset should connect now. (adb did not report back, which is normal on the PICO.)
usb_connect_timeout_short: The headset is not answering adb.
usb_connect_timeout:
The headset did not answer adb within the waiting time.

On a PICO 4 this is almost always the USB interface stuck in file transfer mode. How to fix it:

1. Put the headset on
2. Open the USB options
3. Switch briefly to "Charge only"
4. Switch straight back to "File transfer"

Then press Connect again — the attempt keeps running for 90 seconds and takes hold as soon as the headset responds.

If that does not help: close any open MTP window in the file manager and replug the cable.
diag_report_copied:
Diagnostics report copied ({lines} lines).

Contains versions, distribution, GPU, OpenXR runtime, adb and firewall state — no log, no IP addresses, paths shortened.
usb_auto_connecting: Headset detected on the cable — connecting automatically...
streaming_usb_autoconnect_self: Yakuda Connect does this itself: as soon as the headset is detected on the cable and the server is running, it connects automatically — no running WiVRn dashboard needed.
obah_no_manifest_hint: ⚠ No OpenVR action file found (searched: {folder} and the Proton prefix). If it lives elsewhere, pick it with "📂 Action file …". Games using OpenXR directly have none — their controls come from the game itself.
obah_pick_manifest_tip: Pick this game's OpenVR action file (actions.json, steamvr_manifest.json or similar) yourself. It is remembered.
obah_clear_manifest_tip: Forget the picked action file and search automatically again
obah_pick_manifest_invalid:
This is not an OpenVR action file (the "actions" list is missing):
{path}
xrb_install_text:
xrBinder is built from source (git, cmake, C++ compiler). Missing tools are installed in the terminal, which may ask for your sudo password. Takes about a minute.

Install now?
xrb_build_failed:
xrBinder could not be built.

Log: {log}
xrb_service_failed: The xrBinder service (ipc_server) could not be started. Remapping still works, but running games will not show up here.
xrb_foreign:
A second xrBinder installation was found (copied by hand?). The layer would be loaded twice:
{paths}

xrb_debug_log_missing:
No log yet. It is created on the next game start (after “Rebuild”):
{path}
xrb_cleanup_done:
The hand-copied xrBinder files are now here:
{path}
xrb_cleanup_system: This file is outside your home folder and is left alone. Please remove it manually.
xrb_hint_no_actions: No actions known for this game yet. Start it once while Yakuda Connect is open.
xrb_hint_running: The game is running: after “Save” a new mapping applies immediately.
xrb_hint_offline: The game is not running: changes apply on its next start.
xrb_result_live: ✓ Saved and applied to the running game.
xrb_result_restart: Saved. Removed mappings apply after restarting {game} (xrBinder cannot remove them live without crashing the game).
xrb_result_next_start: Saved. Applies on the next start of {game}.
xrb_card_desc: Remap buttons for OpenXR games without SteamVR bindings (e.g. Unreal games under Proton). The games appear in the game list below with “· OpenXR”.
xrb_game_tip: OpenXR game — buttons are remapped in the background by xrBinder
xrb_hint_disabled_card: xrBinder is off — switch on the “xrBinder” card above, then start the game.
xrb_card_hint: Click a button: assign or disable functions
xrb_editor_status: OpenXR · xrBinder  ·  {bound} of {total} buttons bound  ·  {changed} changed
xrb_reset_all_tip: Undo all remappings for this game
xrb_template_tip: The game reports no buttons. Creates a common default layout (trigger, grip, sticks, buttons) – active only after “Save”, “Discard” undoes it.
xrb_template_none: None of the game's functions match the template. Bind buttons by clicking a card.
xrb_template_applied: Template: {matched} of {total} functions assigned – check and save
xrb_hint_template: The game reports no buttons (e.g. VRChat via xrizer). “🧩 Use OpenXR template” creates a default layout.
xrb_reset_all_text: Undo all remappings for {game}? Nothing is written until you click “Save”.
xrb_obah_hint_xr: Does the game use OpenXR (e.g. Unreal)? Switch on xrBinder above and start it — it then appears here with “· OpenXR”.

xrd_not_available: The game's controller profile does not provide this button right now
xrd_other_tip: Has no button on the detected controller — usually meant for another controller

notice_xrb_missing: xrBinder is not installed — without it OpenXR games cannot be remapped. Please install it.
notice_xrb_off: xrBinder is off — remappings for OpenXR games only apply once it is switched on.
notice_xrb_rebuild: xrBinder needs a rebuild so remappings reach the game.
xrd_tilt_threshold_tip: How far the stick must be tilted to count. Raise it if the stick drifts (triggers on its own).
xrd_tilt_tip: Also triggers when the stick is only tilted — no need to click it (e.g. for selecting and snap turn in older games).
xrd_deadzone_tip: Small movements around the center count as “stick at rest” – against stick drift (character walks or turns on its own).
xrd_deadzone_value_tip: How far the stick must move before the game sees it. Raise it if the stick still drifts.

xrd_deadzone_none: No stick direction of the game on this stick.
xrd_deadzone_differs: Left and right are set differently – moving this slider sets both the same.
xrb_result_restart_axis: Saved. Deadzone/tilt take effect after restarting {game} (changing them live makes xrBinder crash the game).
xrb_obah_hint_running: ▶ Running as OpenXR right now: {games} — it's a separate entry with “· OpenXR” in the game list above. Remap it there.
xrb_bindings_guessed: assuming xrizer's default layout (the runtime reports no buttons)
cli_restart_ask: The server is running. Restart it now so this takes effect?
cli_restart_hint: Takes effect after a server restart (YC-wivrn-toggle twice).
cli_no_server_binary: wivrn-server was not found. Is WiVRn installed?
cli_help_status: Shows server, OpenVR, encoder and graphics card
cli_help_toggle: WiVRn server on/off (whichever it is now)
cli_help_encoder: Choose encoder (Auto, nvenc, vaapi, Vulkan, x264)
cli_help_gpu: Choose the graphics card for WiVRn
cli_help_footer: Without a number you get asked. With a number it applies right away, e.g. YC-encoder 2 or YC-encoder vaapi.
cli_group_desc: Use Yakuda Connect without the GUI — saves RAM in VR (no Qt). Commands: YC-help, YC-status, YC-wivrn-toggle, YC-openvr, YC-encoder, YC-GPU, YC-killapps, YC-autostart-reset, YC-pairing.
cli_setup_tip: Creates the YC-* commands, matching how you installed (AUR, curl, AppImage, source).
cli_open_tip: Opens the terminal menu and closes the GUI. The WiVRn server keeps running.
cli_setup_system: The commands are already installed (they come with the {kind} package). Just type YC-help in a terminal.
cli_setup_skipped: Not created, another program already uses the name: {names}
cli_setup_path:
{dir} is not in your PATH. Add this line to ~/.bashrc (or ~/.zshrc) and open a new terminal:

export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
cli_setup_appimage: AppImage note: the commands point to this file. After moving it or updating, press the button again.
cli_open_confirm:
Start terminal mode?

The GUI will close to save RAM. The WiVRn server keeps running. To get the GUI back, start yakuda-connect normally.
cli_no_terminal:
No terminal program found. You can start the mode yourself with:

{cmd}
cli_autostart_armed: Autostart is waiting for the headset — programs start as soon as it connects.
cli_autostart_none: No autostart programs set up (in the GUI under Dashboard → Autostart).
cli_help_autostart_reset: Reset start timer: programs start again on next connect
cli_help_pairing: Enable pairing and show the PIN
cli_pairing_no_wivrnctl: wivrnctl was not found. Is WiVRn installed?
cli_pairing_hint: Enter the PIN in the headset. Enter or Ctrl+C ends pairing.
autostart_vr_hint: Starts as soon as the headset connects.
autostart_profile_gap_tip: Wait time between two programs — they start one after another instead of all at once (easier on performance while e.g. VRChat loads). 0 = all at once.
autostart_profile_status_headset: {trigger} is running — waiting for the headset.
cli_profiles_armed: Autostart profiles are being watched (game + headset).
autostart_profiles_hint: A profile starts its programs when the chosen game runs AND the headset is connected — and closes them again. The switch turns this automation on for all profiles; the big buttons always work.
autostart_profiles_empty: No profile yet — create one with “＋ New profile” (e.g. “VRChat”: VRCX + OSC tools).
autostart_profile_status_master_off: Automation off (switch above) — programs only via “▶ Start programs”.
autostart_profile_stop_now_tip: Closes this profile's programs right away.
